# zlantp

> Returns the norm of a complex triangular matrix in packed storage.

<section class="usage">

## Usage

```js
import zlantp from '@rreusser/blahpack/lapack/base/zlantp';
```

### Layout API

Takes a storage layout (`order`) and leading dimensions, like CBLAS/LAPACKE.

```js
zlantp( order, norm, uplo, diag, N, AP, WORK ) → number
```

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `order` | `Layout` | Storage layout<br>One of `'row-major'`, `'column-major'`. |
| `norm` | `"one-norm" \| "max" \| "inf-norm" \| "frobenius"` | `'max'`, `'one-norm'`, `'inf-norm'`, or `'frobenius'` |
| `uplo` | `MatrixTriangle` | Specifies whether the upper or lower triangle is stored (`'upper'` or `'lower'`) |
| `diag` | `DiagonalType` | Specifies whether the matrix has a unit diagonal (`'unit'` or `'non-unit'`) |
| `N` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Order of the matrix |
| `AP` | `Complex128Array`<br><sub>length trunc(N * (N + 1) / 2)</sub> | Packed triangular matrix, length >= N\*(N+1)/2 |
| `WORK` | `Float64Array \| null` | **out** · Workspace array, length >= N |

<details>
<summary>Reference notes for each argument (the reference implementation's own documentation; 1-based indices)</summary>

- `norm`: Specifies the value to be returned in ZLANTP as described above.
- `uplo`: Specifies whether the matrix A is upper or lower triangular.

  -   `= 'U'`: Upper triangular
  -   `= 'L'`: Lower triangular
- `diag`: Specifies whether or not the matrix A is unit triangular.

  -   `= 'N'`: Non-unit triangular
  -   `= 'U'`: Unit triangular
- `N`: The order of the matrix A. $N \ge 0$. When $N = 0$, ZLANTP is set to zero.
- `AP`: The upper or lower triangular matrix A, packed columnwise in a linear array. The j-th column of A is stored in the array `AP` as follows: if `UPLO = 'U'`, `AP(i + (j-1)*j/2) = A(i,j)` for $1 \le i \le j$; if `UPLO = 'L'`, `AP(i + (j-1)*(2n-j)/2) = A(i,j)` for $j \le i \le n$. Note that when `DIAG = 'U'`, the elements of the array `AP` corresponding to the diagonal elements of the matrix A are not referenced, but are assumed to be one.
- `WORK`: where $\mathrm{LWORK} \ge N$ when `NORM = 'I'`; otherwise, `WORK` is not referenced.

</details>

**Returns** `number`: norm value

**Throws**

- `TypeError` first argument must be a valid order
- `TypeError` second argument must be one of the following: "one-norm", "max", "inf-norm", "frobenius"
- `TypeError` third argument must be a valid matrix triangle
- `TypeError` fourth argument must be a valid diagonal type

### Strided (ndarray) API

Takes explicit strides and offsets for every array. Use it for views, sub-matrices and non-unit strides.

```js
zlantp.ndarray(
    norm, uplo, diag,
    N,
    AP, strideAP, offsetAP,
    WORK, strideWork, offsetWork
) → number
```

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `norm` | `"one-norm" \| "max" \| "inf-norm" \| "frobenius"` | Specifies the norm: `'max'`, `'one-norm'`, `'inf-norm'`, or `'frobenius'` |
| `uplo` | `MatrixTriangle` | Specifies whether the upper or lower triangle is stored (`'upper'` or `'lower'`) |
| `diag` | `DiagonalType` | Specifies whether the matrix has a unit diagonal (`'unit'` or `'non-unit'`) |
| `N` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Order of the matrix |
| `AP` | `Complex128Array`<br><sub>length trunc(N * (N + 1) / 2)</sub> | Packed triangular matrix |
| ↳ `strideAP` | `integer` | Stride length for `AP` (in complex elements) |
| ↳ `offsetAP` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Starting index for `AP` (in complex elements) |
| `WORK` | `Float64Array` | **out** · Workspace array (length >= N when norm is `'inf-norm'`) |
| ↳ `strideWork` | `integer` | Stride length for `WORK` |
| ↳ `offsetWork` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Starting index for `WORK` |

<details>
<summary>Reference notes for each argument (the reference implementation's own documentation; 1-based indices)</summary>

- `norm`: Specifies the value to be returned in ZLANTP as described above.
- `uplo`: Specifies whether the matrix A is upper or lower triangular.

  -   `= 'U'`: Upper triangular
  -   `= 'L'`: Lower triangular
- `diag`: Specifies whether or not the matrix A is unit triangular.

  -   `= 'N'`: Non-unit triangular
  -   `= 'U'`: Unit triangular
- `N`: The order of the matrix A. $N \ge 0$. When $N = 0$, ZLANTP is set to zero.
- `AP`: The upper or lower triangular matrix A, packed columnwise in a linear array. The j-th column of A is stored in the array `AP` as follows: if `UPLO = 'U'`, `AP(i + (j-1)*j/2) = A(i,j)` for $1 \le i \le j$; if `UPLO = 'L'`, `AP(i + (j-1)*(2n-j)/2) = A(i,j)` for $j \le i \le n$. Note that when `DIAG = 'U'`, the elements of the array `AP` corresponding to the diagonal elements of the matrix A are not referenced, but are assumed to be one.
- `WORK`: where $\mathrm{LWORK} \ge N$ when `NORM = 'I'`; otherwise, `WORK` is not referenced.

</details>

**Returns** `number`: norm value

**Throws**

- `TypeError` first argument must be one of the following: "one-norm", "max", "inf-norm", "frobenius"
- `TypeError` second argument must be a valid matrix triangle
- `TypeError` third argument must be a valid diagonal type

</section>

<section class="notes">

## Notes

-   `zlantp()` corresponds to the reference LAPACK routine [`ZLANTP`](https://github.com/Reference-LAPACK/lapack/blob/v3.12.0/SRC/zlantp.f).

</section>

<section class="examples">

## Examples

```js
import Complex128Array from '@stdlib/array/complex128/lib/index.js';
import Float64Array from '@stdlib/array/float64/lib/index.js';
import zlantp from '@rreusser/blahpack/lapack/base/zlantp';

/*
* 3x3 upper triangular matrix (packed):
*   A = [ (1+2i) (3+4i) (5+6i) ]
*       [     0  (7+8i) (9+1i) ]
*       [     0      0  (2+3i) ]
*/
const AP = new Complex128Array( [ 1.0, 2.0, 3.0, 4.0, 7.0, 8.0, 5.0, 6.0, 9.0, 1.0, 2.0, 3.0 ] ); // eslint-disable-line max-len
const WORK = new Float64Array( 3 );

console.log( 'Max norm (upper, non-unit):', zlantp( 'column-major', 'max', 'upper', 'non-unit', 3, AP, WORK ) ); // eslint-disable-line max-len
console.log( 'One norm (upper, non-unit):', zlantp( 'column-major', 'one-norm', 'upper', 'non-unit', 3, AP, WORK ) ); // eslint-disable-line max-len
console.log( 'Inf norm (upper, non-unit):', zlantp( 'column-major', 'inf-norm', 'upper', 'non-unit', 3, AP, WORK ) ); // eslint-disable-line max-len
console.log( 'Frobenius norm (upper, non-unit):', zlantp( 'column-major', 'frobenius', 'upper', 'non-unit', 3, AP, WORK ) ); // eslint-disable-line max-len
```

</section>

<!-- /.examples -->

<section class="reference-notes">

## Reference notes

The mathematical description from the reference LAPACK 3.12.0 source of `ZLANTP`. Indices are the 1-based Fortran indices of the source.

### Purpose

ZLANTP returns the value of the one norm, or the Frobenius norm, or the infinity norm, or the element of largest absolute value of a triangular matrix A, supplied in packed form.

### Returns

$$
\mathrm{ZLANTP} = \begin{cases} \max (\lvert A(i,j) \rvert) & \text{NORM = 'M' or 'm'} \\ \mathrm{norm1}(A) & \text{NORM = '1', 'O' or 'o'} \\ \mathrm{normI}(A) & \text{NORM = 'I' or 'i'} \\ \mathrm{normF}(A) & \text{NORM = 'F', 'f', 'E' or 'e'} \end{cases}
$$

where norm1 denotes the one norm of a matrix (maximum column sum), normI denotes the infinity norm of a matrix (maximum row sum) and normF denotes the Frobenius norm of a matrix (square root of sum of squares). Note that max(abs(A(i,j))) is not a consistent matrix norm.

</section>

<!-- /.reference-notes -->
